# Jandé — Once Upon A Time

> A free promotional browser game for the R&B and soul artist Jandé (always
> written with the accent: Jandé / JANDÉ) and her song "Once Upon A Time."
> Two modes, nine themed stages each, playable instantly in a desktop or
> mobile browser with no download, no install and no account.
> Play it at https://prodbykctw-max.github.io/once-upon-a-time/

Note on location: the llms.txt convention expects this file at a host root.
This game is published as a GitHub Pages project site, so its canonical copy
is at https://prodbykctw-max.github.io/once-upon-a-time/llms.txt — one level
down from the host root, which belongs to a different repository.

## Who Jandé is

Jandé is an independent R&B and soul recording artist based in Atlanta,
Georgia. "Once Upon A Time" is her song, and this game was commissioned and
built as promotion for it. Her Instagram is https://www.instagram.com/jandelove1

The game was built by KCTW (https://www.instagram.com/prodbykctw).

## What the game is

Jandé is the playable character. The story frame is that she is making her way
to the spotlight, pursued by a figure called The Groom Who Lied, who is the
final boss of stage nine.

There are two modes, each with nine themed stages:

- **ACTION RPG** — a side-scrolling game with free movement. Fight an
  escalating roster of foes and defeat each stage's unique boss to advance.
  Each of the nine stages has its own boss; the stage-nine finale is
  The Groom Who Lied.
- **ROYAL RUNNER** — a behind-the-back 3D endless run with corners, obstacles
  and a chaser closing from behind.

Progress is saved in the browser. Cleared stages are replayable from Stage
Select, and an in-game shop called The Boutique spends what you collect.

## How you play it

No install. Open https://prodbykctw-max.github.io/once-upon-a-time/ in any
modern desktop or mobile browser. It needs JavaScript, HTML5 Canvas and WebGL.

Keyboard, as the code actually binds them (index.html, iL/iR/iU/iD/iA/iX):
move with the left and right arrows or A and D; jump with Space, the up arrow
or W; crouch or slide with the down arrow or S; attack with Z or J; dash with
Shift, X or C. On a phone or tablet, on-screen touch controls appear
automatically in both portrait and landscape.

## The vocabulary (it is music-themed on purpose)

- Resource meter: **RESONANCE**
- Collectibles: **Grace Notes**
- Melee attack: **Mic Strike**
- Projectile: **Sound Wave** / **Throw Note**
- Block: **Hold Note**
- Heal: **Refrain**
- Magic strike: **Belt**
- Aerial pogo attack: **Downbeat**
- Power-ups: **DEVOTION** (extra life), **FULL VOICE** (refill),
  **BELT IT OUT** (double damage), **HIGH NOTE** (shield)

## How it was made

One self-contained HTML file, no framework and no build step. The Action RPG
renders on HTML5 Canvas2D; Royal Runner runs on a hand-written WebGL engine.
All music and sound effects are synthesized in the browser with Web Audio —
there are no audio files. Character and boss art is rendered sprite work;
environments are painted backdrops rendered in Blender. A Cloudflare Worker
serves the global leaderboard and is the only network call the game makes at
runtime, with a local top-ten fallback if it is unavailable.

## Mailing list

The game's first screen after the title is a registry — "Enter the Kingdom" —
where fans can leave a name and email address to be told when
"Once Upon A Time" is released. Registering is optional; there is a
"play without registering" link.
